title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned the teacher's week-to-view planner. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Week-to-view planner
options.lineage: The A4 teacher's planner: cloth cover, week-to-view spread, ribbon marker
options.thesis: Your timetable as the planner you'd buy every August, with a ribbon on now.
options.viewport: Cobalt cloth side rail; ruled period rows across five day columns, lessons carrying class-colour edge tabs, a red ribbon down today's column to now.
options.risk: Planner furniture can tip into costume if the ruling gets heavier than the data.

raised.raise: Today steps down a fixed size ramp: now, next, later.
One region dominates each screen: the open lesson owns its half.
The class code is one form at every scale: tab, cell, page title.
Opening a lesson dims the rest of the week.
Period numbers are the index, set large and tabular at the head of every row.

options.label: Jotter covers
options.lineage: Scottish school jotters: coloured covers, printed label box, feint ruling and red margin
options.thesis: Every class is a jotter in its own colour; notes go on the feint lines inside.
options.viewport: Week grid on white, each lesson a small jotter-cover block; the open class shows its label box and notes on feint lines with dates in the red margin.
options.risk: The most familiar school-stationery reading; feint ruling can feel like dress-up.

options.label: Departures board
options.thesis: Today is a departures board: every period a row, now in amber.
options.viewport: Black board with fixed columns time, period, class, note; amber lamp on the current row; notes open in a steel-framed panel.
options.case: Wins clarity for now and next; loses on audience, since teachers don't see their day as a station.
options.risk: A black board is heavy for writing long notes.

options.label: Star atlas
options.thesis: Lessons as stars sized by importance.
options.viewport: A week plotted as a star field.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a timetable is not a sky.
options.kept: A fixed size ramp carries hierarchy.

options.label: Zoo guide map
options.thesis: Each class a coloured lobe of land.
options.viewport: The week as a map of class islands.
options.case: Fuses poorly: periods are a grid, not a coastline.

options.label: Bitmap specimen
options.thesis: Class codes as pixel display type.
options.viewport: Huge pixel class code over dense columns.
options.case: Fuses poorly: no tie to school life.
options.kept: One form repeated at every scale.

options.label: Streaming wall
options.thesis: Classes as rows of poster tiles.
options.viewport: Rows of lessons per class, focus expands.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a week is days by periods, not rows of content.

options.label: Catalog sleeve
options.thesis: Everything numbered; colour codes stand in for names.
options.viewport: Period numbers as the only headlines.
options.case: Fuses poorly: hiding class names hurts a glance.
options.kept: One numbering system is the index.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean calendar-app week view, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Top bar with week switcher, white day-by-period grid with tinted class blocks, blue now line, right-hand notes drawer.
canonCard.risk: Looks like every calendar app by design.
